Options 0 and 3 reflect crude archival literalism (filtering only archive-confirmed memories or treating all memories as facts), and option 2 asserts a convergence of accounts that contradicts the premise of ‘contradictory’ testimonies. I assign high probability to 1 while leaving modest probability to 2 (possible if the historian aims to show eventual agreement) and small probabilities to 0 and 3.
